text:
maya: Quick sync — I'm sketching the Console wizard for creating A/B experiments (variants, routing rules, quota buckets). Need to lock down how we express guards and ramping in the UI vs the API.
jon: +1. Are we supporting time-based ramps (0->50% over 30m) or only discrete steps? Keep in mind Dedicated customers may want scheduled ramps.
sophia: We should support both. UI can show a simple slider for quick canaries and an \"advanced ramp\" mode for schedules. Implementation: API accepts either a single traffic split or an array of (ts, pct) windows.
aleks: Heads-up: runtime routing expects a deterministic routing_policy object. If we accept an array it needs to compile to a per-minute policy or a small DSL the router can interpret. Prefer a compact ramp spec in the experiment resource.
product-ana: For UX, we want a one-click canary experience for product teams. Default to 5% for 15m then 20% for 1h, unless they pick custom.
jon: Default sounds good. Also: what about guard thresholds? We need sensible defaults so folks don't shoot themselves in the foot.
maya: Proposal: two guard types — safety guards (hard) and observation guards (soft). Safety guards enforce immediate rollback/fallback when key metrics cross thresholds. Observation guards just flag and notify.
sophia: Example safety guard rules: error_rate_increase_pct > 100% (relative) for 5m OR absolute_error_rate > 0.02 for 3m => immediate rollback. Latency p95 degrade > 200ms absolute or > 30% relative => rollback. Those seem reasonable defaults.
aleks: Agree but we must keep the evaluation inexpensive. Router will evaluate metrics coming from the telemetry aggregator every 10s and compare to baseline stored in experiment.metadata.baseline_metrics.
maya: Let's include a small example config for the API that Console will create (this will be printed to logs and editable in JSON mode):

```
{
  "experiment_id": "exp_console_2026_03_12",
  "variants": [
    {"id": "control", "model": "redwood/small", "pct": 80},
    {"id": "v1", "model": "redwood/small-quant", "pct": 20}
  ],
  "ramp": [
    {"after": "0m", "split": {"control": 95, "v1": 5}},
    {"after": "15m", "split": {"control": 80, "v1": 20}}
  ],
  "guards": {
    "safety": [
      {"metric": "error_rate", "type": "relative", "threshold_pct": 100, "window": "5m"},
      {"metric": "latency_p95_ms", "type": "absolute", "threshold": 200, "window": "3m"}
    ],
    "observation": [
      {"metric": "cost_per_1000", "type": "absolute", "threshold": 5.00, "window": "1h"}
    ]
  },
  "telemetry_tags": ["console_experiment","team:search"]
}
```

jon: Nice. One subtlety: error_rate relative comparisons need a stable baseline. We should capture a baseline window (e.g., 2h pre-rollout) and store it in experiment.baseline. If insufficient baseline data, fall back to absolute thresholds.
sophia: Agreed. Also let's make the baseline capture optional for quick experiments (checkbox: \"Use historical baseline\"). If unchecked, we only use absolutes.
product-ana: For the Console: show a preview panel that simulates the ramp and highlights when each safety guard would trip for historical traffic. That would help PMs understand risk before starting.
maya: Good idea. We can run a dry-run using archived traces to simulate traffic distribution and compute hypothetical guard triggers. We already have a simulator in eng-ml infra — call it from the Console backend.
aleks: Implementation note: the router needs a compact runtime representation. Suggest we compile ramps into a list of (start_ts, split_map) and guards into normalized expressions. Avoid freeform JS in experiments.
jon: Also quota enforcement — experiments must respect route-level quota limits. If someone tries to send 30% to a variant with 0 capacity we should block the experiment creation and show a helpful message.
sophia: We should integrate the quota check into the experiment validation endpoint and surface which capacity pool is insufficient. e.g., \"Dedicated pool: us-west-2-gpu-nvlink - insufficient availability for requested peak QPS\".
maya: For telemetry events, let's standardize names so downstream analytics can pick up: experiment.start, experiment.step, experiment.guard.trigger, experiment.rollback, experiment.finish. Include variant traffic map and guard_id in payload.
product-ana: Also include user.id and reason fields for any manual rollbacks.
jon: On the API debate — should experiments be resources under /projects/:id/experiments or under /routes/:id/experiments? I vote for route-scoped since routing rules often reference routes and quotas.
aleks: Route-scoped is simpler for enforcement, but project-scoped is nicer for UI discovery across routes. Maybe support both: canonical experiments are route-scoped; Console can show cross-route experiments via an index endpoint that aggregates.
maya: Agreed. Keep canonical route-scoped. Console will have a global experiments list with filters.
sophia: One more: audit logs. Every automatic rollback or guard trigger should create an immutable audit entry with before/after traffic maps and metric snapshots.
maya: I'll sketch the Console screens and a minimal API contract. I'll add a PR to the platform repo with the experiment validator and a simulator endpoint. Putting a note: default canary = 5% x 15m -> 20% x1h -> 50% x12h -> drain. We can tune defaults later.
product-ana: Love it. Can you drop the Figma link and the API proto in #eng-platform later?
maya: Yup, will post mock and open a draft PR. Thanks everyone :raised_hands:
deploy-bot: experiment exp_console_2026_03_12 created in staging by maya — status: validating (dry-run)
jon: When you open the PR please include unit tests for validator edge cases (no baseline, quota failure, overlapping ramps, invalid pct sum).
maya: Will do. Closing the loop — I'll post updates in this thread when PR lands.
